findings.source_quote: τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν ἀναδέξασθαι χάριν οἶδα εἰληφώς, οὐ δεδωκώς
findings.english_quote: in undertaking the task of having you administer, I know that I have received a favor, not given one.
findings.issue: The draft makes the speaker undertake the task of having Clement administer. A more direct analysis takes σέ as the subject of ἀναδέξασθαι and οἰκονομεῖν as its complement: Clement undertakes administration, and the speaker receives a favor thereby. The draft's added commissioning construction is not established by the Greek.
findings.suggested_revision: Candidate requiring fresh review: “Hence I know that, in your undertaking to administer, I have received a favor, not given one.” Explain the competing infinitival constructions rather than presenting only the speaker-as-subject interpretation.

findings.issue: Unresolved source/meaning issue: the draft marks this construction as publication-blocking. The alternative syntactic analysis above is a proposal, not independent evidence establishing a final rendering. The image-checked print establishes the supplied words, not their interpretation; no textual corruption is demonstrated.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the publication block pending an independently supported syntactic analysis identifying the subjects and complements of both infinitives. Preserve the supplied reading and document the alternative analysis. Do not seek to resolve this merely by removing the unrelated apostrophe before σωτηρίας.

findings.issue: χριστοῦ functions independently as a title, not within a personal-name construction. The supplied POB policy calls for “Messiah” here.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace “from Christ” with “from the Messiah,” subject to fresh review.

findings.issue: The verb explicitly evokes hunting. “Pursue” weakens that image in the main translation, although the lexical note recognizes it.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare “hunt for the beneficial praise that comes from the Messiah” as the source-transparent candidate, preserving the contrast with shaking off praise arising from injustice.

findings.source_quote: χριστόν, οὗ τὴν καθέδραν πεπίστευται, οὐκ ἐδέξατο, καὶ ’ὡς χριστὸν μὴ δεξάμενος
findings.english_quote: has not received Christ, whose chair has been entrusted to him; and as one who has not received Christ
findings.issue: Both occurrences of χριστός are independently titular. Neither belongs to a personal-name construction supporting the policy exception “Christ.” The printed apostrophe before ὡς is a disclosed orthographic feature, not an unresolved meaning problem.
findings.suggested_revision: Use “has not received the Messiah, whose chair has been entrusted to him; and as one who has not received the Messiah.” Preserve both negations and the entrusted-chair image. The replacement requires fresh review.

findings.english_quote: seeking to have everyone as friends
findings.issue: The middle participle carries a claim-pressing or assertion nuance that generic “seeking” does not express. The lexical note recognizes this nuance without preserving it in the translation.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare “pressing his claim to have everyone as friends” as a candidate for fresh review. This lexical proposal does not resolve the following pronoun and reconciliation uncertainties.

findings.issue: Unresolved source/meaning issue: the draft explicitly leaves the antecedent of αὐτόν and the precise force of active διαλλάττων unsettled and marks them publication-blocking. Referring to the presiding leader and referring to the alienated person produce materially different accounts of the reconciliation. The supplied print does not settle this interpretive question.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the block until an independently supported discourse analysis and lexical account of διαλλάττων justify the chosen relationship. Preserve the alternative antecedents and the possibilities of reconciling, winning over, or effecting reconciliation with the referent. Do not present a proposed interpretation as accepted.

findings.issue: Unresolved source/meaning issue: the draft identifies the antecedent of αὐτοῦ as uncertain and publication-blocking. Its identification with the presiding leader is plausible but remains a disclosed choice rather than an independently established resolution.
findings.suggested_revision: Supply an independently supported antecedent analysis connecting this possessive with the preceding reconciliation clause. Until then, retain the neutral pronoun and the alternative-reference note. This is interpretive uncertainty, not evidence of defective transcription.

findings.issue: The draft omits ἔξωθεν, “from outside.” Openness does not convey external location or affiliation. The omission also obscures the contrast with τοὺς ἔσω, “those within,” at the sentence's end.
findings.suggested_revision: Use “the obvious enemies from outside,” or another rendering explicitly preserving both their manifest enmity and their position outside. Review the revised sentence afresh.

findings.source_quote: σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι ἐν ἐπιτομῇ ἀναγραψάμενον
findings.issue: The source note overstates the case against σέ. It can resume the earlier σε as the accusative subject of διαπέμψαι, with ἀναγραψάμενον agreeing with that subject. It therefore need not mean that Clement himself is the object being sent. The proposed correction to σύ is not established by the supplied reading.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain σέ and remove any implication that σὺ is an established correction. Explain the resumptive accusative analysis separately from the remaining difficulty of the extended sentence. The main rendering “send James ... a concise written account” does not require replacement solely because of σέ.

findings.source_quote: Ἀξιῶ σε ... ὅπως ὁπόταν ... σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι ... δηλῶσαι μὴ ὀκνήσῃς
findings.issue: Unresolved source/meaning issue: the extended request moves between Ἀξιῶ σε, ὅπως, an accusative-and-infinitive construction, and the concluding prohibition. The resumptive-accusative proposal does not independently establish the construction of the entire sentence or clear the draft's publication-blocking syntax issue. No corrupt printed word has been demonstrated.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the block pending an independently supported grammatical analysis of the whole request, including the relation of ὅπως to the infinitives and μὴ ὀκνήσῃς. Preserve the supplied wording; do not substitute σύ or import another edition's construction.

findings.source_quote: ὃ πάντως ἔδει με παθεῖν εὐσεβῶς ἀπεδόμην
findings.english_quote: I have piously paid what I was in every way bound to suffer.
findings.issue: Here πάντως reinforces the certainty or inevitability of the necessary suffering. “In every way” instead suggests necessity in every respect or manner, obscuring the connection with the unavoidable death under discussion.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare “I have piously paid what I was inevitably bound to suffer.” Retain the obligation/payment language and subject the candidate to fresh review.

findings.source_quote: οὐκ ἀμαθὴς ἀνὴρ καὶ ζωοποιοὺς λόγους ἀγνοῶν καὶ ἐκκλησίας κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς
findings.english_quote: not to an unlearned man ignorant of life-giving words and unacquainted with the church’s rule.
findings.issue: Unresolved source/meaning issue: the draft marks the scope of the first οὐκ across the coordinated descriptions as publication-blocking. Its collective-negation interpretation is plausible, but the note leaves that scope unresolved. The second οὐκ belongs to the description “not knowing” the church's rule and must remain represented. The printed period is an editorial feature, not by itself evidence of corruption.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the block until an independently supported scope analysis explains how the coordinated descriptions relate to the first negation and the later finite verb. Preserve both negations and document the chosen collective-scope reading without treating removal of the printed period as a textual correction.

findings.source_quote: Κλήμεντος τῶν Πέτρου ἐπιδημίων κηρυγμάτων ἐπιτομή
findings.english_quote: Clement’s Epitome of Peter’s Preachings during His Sojourns
findings.issue: Unresolved source/meaning issue: ἐπιδημίων adjectivally qualifies κηρυγμάτων. The draft expands that relationship into preachings delivered during Peter's sojourns, while its note preserves visit-associated and local/public interpretations and marks the issue publication-blocking. The sojourn rendering is plausible, but lexical fidelity cannot be certified while that gate remains unresolved. This is not demonstrated source corruption.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the title unresolved pending independent lexical and contextual evidence for ἐπιδήμιος modifying κηρύγματα in this setting. Compare the sojourn/visit rendering explicitly with a local-preachings rendering, retaining the alternatives in the notes. Any selected replacement must undergo fresh review.
